findings.title: Busy times are ignored for any slot on a day that has a date override
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, after the date-override block, `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` returns early and completely skips the `busy.every(...)` check below. Consequence: on any day for which the host has a date override, existing bookings and external calendar busy times are no longer taken into account, so already-booked slots are offered again and can be double booked. The early return should only mean "working-hours check is superseded by the override"; the busy-time check must still run.

findings.title: Working-hours check is inverted: any non-matching range marks the slot unavailable
findings.body: The new check uses `workingHours.find(wh => slot is OUTSIDE wh)` and returns `false` (unavailable) if such an entry is found. A user whose schedule has more than one availability block on the same weekday (e.g. 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, the normal "lunch break" setup) will always have at least one block that does not contain the slot, so *every* slot on that day is rejected. Fixed hosts / collective events with split availability will show no slots at all. The logic must be "available if the slot fits inside at least one working-hour range for that day" (e.g. `!workingHours.some(covers)`).

findings.title: `end` computed from slot start instead of slot end in working-hours check
findings.body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` duplicates the `start` expression; it should be derived from `slotEndTime`. As written the event length is ignored, so a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after them passes the `end > workingHour.endTime` test. The variable is dead/duplicated code that makes the guard weaker than intended.

findings.title: Multiple date overrides on the same day make all slots unavailable
findings.body: `dateOverrides.find(...)` returns truthy as soon as *one* override on the slot's day does not contain the slot, and the code then returns `false` (unavailable). Users can define several override ranges for the same date (e.g. 09:00–10:00 and 14:00–15:00). With two ranges, a slot inside the first range is still rejected by the second, so no slot on that date is bookable. The check must be "unavailable only if the slot fits none of the day's overrides".

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with `===`, condition never true
findings.body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly created Dayjs objects by reference, so it is always false. The intended case (zero-length override, i.e. a date marked fully unavailable) is therefore never detected and the code falls through to the range comparisons, where a slot starting exactly at the override instant is reported as available. Use `.isSame(...)`.

findings.title: Date-override day comparison is done in the server's local timezone
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` builds a Dayjs in the *server's local* timezone, while `slotStartTime` is `time.utc()` and formats in UTC. On any deployment whose process timezone is not UTC, the two date strings can differ by a day, so the override silently does not match the slot and `dateOverrideExist` stays false, falling back to normal working hours and ignoring the override entirely. Use `dayjs.utc(date.start)` for the comparison. The same conversion also shifts overrides whose local time is near midnight onto the neighbouring UTC day, where they will never match a slot.

findings.title: `override.timeZone` is optional; undefined falls back to the server timezone
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` relies on `TimeRange.timeZone`, which was added as optional in `packages/types/schedule.d.ts`. When a caller of `getSlots` passes date overrides without `timeZone` (every call site other than the tRPC `getSchedule` that was updated in this PR), `.tz(undefined)` silently uses the process default timezone, producing a wrong `organizerUtcOffset` and therefore slots shifted by an arbitrary amount. Either make the field required on the type used by `GetSlots` or fall back explicitly to the organizer timezone.

findings.title: Override converted to minutes-of-day wraps across midnight and lands on the wrong day
findings.body: `startTime`/`endTime` are computed as `hour()*60 + minute()` after shifting the override by `offset`. When the shift crosses midnight (e.g. an override at 22:00–23:00 organizer time viewed from a timezone 2 hours ahead becomes 00:00–01:00 of the next day), the minute-of-day values wrap: the override is then applied to the *current* invitee day at the wrong clock time, or produces `startTime > endTime` which `buildSlots` discards, dropping the availability completely. Overrides must be attributed to the invitee day they actually fall on rather than being collapsed to minutes-of-day of the day being iterated.

findings.title: No test for the main fix (date overrides of fixed hosts in round-robin)
findings.body: The PR's primary claim is that date overrides of fixed hosts are now honoured for ROUND_ROBIN events, but the only new test asserts that the existing single-user override case returns the same UTC slots for a second invitee timezone. There is no scenario with a ROUND_ROBIN event type, a fixed host with a date override and an available non-fixed host, so the new `checkIfIsAvailable` override/working-hours code path (and the regression it can cause for split availability or for days with both an override and an existing booking) is untested.
